title: VOF phase transport versus mixture FaceFlux: diagnostic review
status: Reporter-only R10 prepared; no new solver run or physical change by reviewer
conclusion: The observed BDF2 density-inventory plus mixture FaceFlux residual remains above its 0.01% threshold. Existing evidence does not yet distinguish transport iteration error from a difference between native phase boundary fluxes and mixture FaceFlux. A reporter-only matched replay is justified before changing solver settings.

confirmed.temporal: Second-order VOF is documented as BDF2. Substeps=1 does not imply first-order transport. Spatial HRIC/face-density order is separate from temporal integration.
confirmed.forcing: VOF wave forcing and damping are momentum-source mechanisms; forcing explicitly has no phase or turbulence sources. Their mere presence is not evidence of an omitted phase mass source.
confirmed.reports: At the saved t=0.750 checkpoint, original and fresh unsmoothed density/volume and boundary MassFlowReport values match. Smoothing and idealization are not the demonstrated explanation there.
confirmed.native_mass_error: The phase-native MassConservationErrorReport sums the phase mass imbalance calculated when solving transport equations over cells and multiplies it by the current physical time step. It is an iteration-error measure in kg per step; divide by dt for kg/s.
confirmed.phase_flow_field: MassFlowRate[phase] represents phase kg/s through a boundary face, with positive outflow. Sum face values without multiplying by area. MassFlux[phase] instead has kg/(m2 s) units and positive inflow; it must not be substituted without sign and area handling.

unresolved: No inspected primary text explicitly establishes that generic FaceFlux equals the sum of HRIC-discretized phase mass fluxes at every boundary and every inner-iteration state.
The phase MassFlowRate field definition does not explicitly identify its temporal/subcycling evaluation stage. Compare it with native equation errors rather than assuming exact discrete equivalence.

The MMP field catalog gives a simplified face-sum definition for MassImbalance[phase], whereas the dedicated native report is explicitly documented as a transport-equation error. Prefer the native report to an inferred volume-integral residual.
FIRST_ORDER face density reconstruction applies to internal faces. It can affect consistency, but it is not alone proof of the origin of a global boundary-budget discrepancy.
The actual boolean getUserSourceOption() of MmpUserSourceOption was missing in the prior reflection audit. R10 reads it explicitly and refuses a source-enabled case.

discrete_comparison.normalized_metric: 100*residual/inward_mixture_mass_kg_s; preserve signed values and report absolute maxima separately
discrete_comparison.cancellation_check: Also record sum of absolute native water/air errors divided by dt and inlet mass, so cancellation between phases is visible.
discrete_comparison.inference: For fixed cell volumes and constant phase densities, mixture inventory is the density-weighted sum of phase volume inventories. A matching discrete budget must use the corresponding phase transport fluxes and source terms. This mathematical identity does not prove which exposed field is the solver-consistent flux.
discrete_comparison.start_handling: Keep checkpoint-load cache separate. Require finite native errors after first physical step. Compute BDF2 only from step 2 of a replay that retains the same dt; do not include a mixed-dt stencil without variable-step coefficients.

recommendation.probe: R10: existing R4 t=0.500 checkpoint, same SO1ms10inner settings, 250 steps to0.750; add reports only.
recommendation.no_change: Do not alter the 0.01% guard, old history, reconstruction, source settings, solver relaxation or physics as part of this diagnostic.
readouts: original raw history and boundary mixture flux
BDF2 inventory with mixture and phase boundary flux variants
phase-source boolean, phase model inventory, report units/parts/representation
native report cache and error logs
decision_rules: If phase-flux inventory balance agrees with native equation error while generic FaceFlux differs, quantify the difference boundary by boundary. Document the diagnostic-definition distinction before proposing a revised acceptance metric.
If both phase-flux and generic budgets reproduce the native phase error peaks, investigate actual phase/continuity coupling and local residuals; do not declare reporting mismatch.
If native reports are invalid or inconsistent after a guarded step, the diagnostic is incomplete; retain the existing block.
A small native iteration error alone does not certify global mass conservation or long-wave propagation accuracy. Keep inventory and gauge/cycle diagnostics.
